coaching.coaching: Plan how verification coverage of the acceptance criteria will be verified in-session — restate any deferred or unobservable success target as an observable proxy.
coaching.subject: verification coverage of the acceptance criteria

metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
verify command `grep -rn 'bak-retarget' src/ .github/` inspects output with `grep` but asserts nothing — add an exit-code or comparison (-q, [ "$(...)" -eq N ], jq -e) so a failure is observable
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a concrete proving command for AC2, e.g. `git cat-file -s <blob-sha-of-prev_snapshot.json>` confirming the removed blob is 33,025,572 bytes, or `du -sh .` before/after `git checkout` on a fresh clone, so the >=33 MB drop is independently measurable.
evidence: AC2 states the expected delta (>=33 MB) but supplies no measurement command (e.g., du -sh after git checkout, or git cat-file --batch-check on the removed blobs)
Taxonomy item 5: missing cardinality/size assertion command when the criterion names a count/size
findings.finding: AC2 ('working-tree size drops by >=33 MB') names a size threshold but provides no proving command to measure it — an executor cannot satisfy or falsify this criterion without knowing what command to run and against what target.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC2: 'Working-tree size of a fresh checkout drops by >=33 MB. Tier: repo measurement.'
scenarios: An executor deletes the directory, runs AC1–AC4, but has no command to prove AC2 — the tier label 'repo measurement' implies a command exists but none is given
A reviewer cannot independently verify the size claim without a stated protocol
findings.suggested_fix: After deletion, run: `git ls-tree -rl HEAD | grep bak-retarget` should return empty (AC1 already covers this); for the size proof add: `git cat-file -s $(git rev-parse HEAD~1:.bridge_state.bak-retarget/prev_snapshot.json)` and assert output equals `33025572`. Alternatively, `du -sh --exclude=.git .` on a fresh clone before vs after the commit and assert delta >=33 MB.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit rollback/back-out statement (e.g., 'revert this commit via `git revert <sha>` on the tickets branch before the epic 0303-692c strip runs') to satisfy T4's reversibility requirement.
evidence: Plan says 'no history rewrite' and 'Immediate working-tree win' but never states how to undo the commit if a downstream issue is found.
T4 criterion: 'The remedy is an explicit rollback/back-out plan or expand-contract — acknowledgement alone is insufficient.'
ABSENCE: no revert instruction, no back-out procedure, no mention of git revert or equivalent.
findings.finding: The plan performs a destructive file-deletion commit but provides no explicit rollback/back-out path. Per T4, acknowledgement of justification is insufficient; the plan must name the reversibility mechanism.
findings.location: Why section / Files section / overall plan
scenarios: Epic 0303-692c's strip step runs and finds unexpected tree-identity mismatch; operator needs to revert this commit quickly but has no documented procedure.
A consumer of .bridge_state.bak-retarget is discovered post-merge (e.g., an external script not covered by the grep scope); rollback path is undefined.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Rollback' sub-section under Why or Files: 'Because this is a plain commit with no history rewrite, the back-out is `git revert <commit-sha>` on the tickets branch. This must be executed before epic 0303-692c's strip step, after which the directory will be absent from history and a revert would re-add it to future checkouts only.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the AC consumer grep to include `scripts/` (e.g., `grep -rn 'bak-retarget' src/ .github/ scripts/`) so the producer directory is explicitly covered.
evidence: Search confirms no hardcoded 'bak-retarget' in scripts/, only the parameterized form
findings.finding: The AC consumer grep (`grep -rn 'bak-retarget' src/ .github/`) omits the `scripts/` directory, which contains the producer script (`scripts/retarget_jira_project.py`) that generates `.bridge_state.bak-<label>` artifacts. While no hardcoded `bak-retarget` string exists there (only the parameterized pattern), the scripts/ tree is an unenumerated consumer scope in the verification step.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC line: `grep -rn 'bak-retarget' src/ .github/` returns no consumer.
scenarios: A future change to scripts/retarget_jira_project.py that hardcodes 'bak-retarget' would not be caught by the stated AC grep.
A reviewer auditing consumers against the AC grep would not discover the producer lives in scripts/ and might miss that the backup pattern is still active.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the AC grep to: `grep -rn 'bak-retarget' src/ .github/ scripts/` returns no hardcoded consumer.
